name: client-repo
description: The docs repo is ours, but the code belongs to a client. The standard's documentation is not written into the client's repo: no versioned pointers, no AGENTS.md, no folders. Only an unversioned CLAUDE.local.md that leads to the docs repo. Working on their code —branches, worktrees, commits— is the assignment and remains normal.
rules: The client's repo is not modified to accommodate this documentation: no versioned pointers, no AGENTS.md, no standard folders. The only thing written is CLAUDE.local.md, excluded from git, which loads the docs repo index when working on the code. If the client's repo already came with its own versioned AGENTS.md, it is respected: it is not ours and is not deleted.
Measurements are recorded, not diagnoses. Nothing is declared a bug and no conclusion is drawn about what is wrong without the client's validation.
Every observation carries reproducible evidence: file and line, or the command or query that demonstrates it. Without evidence it is not written.
What was measured is always distinguished from what is inherited from prior documentation: documents describe the intent at the time they were written, not the current state.
Project notes and references go to git, not to the agent's local memory.

The description of a change proposal says what changes, what is added and why, plus what was checked and what is pending. It does not name our tooling —crux, its commands, its skills, its markers— nor our branch names or internal processes: the reader does not know how we work inside and it adds nothing for them. The client's own repo scripts are cited, because they are theirs.

forbid.reason: this names our tooling in a client's repo
